name: Toshiko Kishida
shortBio: Meiji-era Japanese feminist philosopher and Freedom and People’s Rights orator whose speech "Daughters in Boxes" critiqued Confucian household confinement as an obstacle to women’s moral autonomy and civic equality.
centralQuestion: How does domestic seclusion ("daughters in boxes") violate natural human rights and stunt women’s intellectual and civic capacities?

keyWorks.title: Daughters in Boxes (Hakoiri Musume)
keyWorks.description: Landmark Meiji feminist lecture critiquing patriarchal familial control and demanding women’s education and political participation.
